title: Summary and review questions
competency: Bring together the ideas of Unit 1.

keywords.def: A person who has specific rights and responsibilities under the law.
Full and responsible membership of the state. It is a legal status and an identity.
Devotion to and strong support for your country.
The ability or willingness to accept opinions or behaviour you disagree with.

en.text: A citizen has rights and obligations under the law. Citizenship is a legal status and an identity. A good citizen obeys the law, is responsible, tolerant and patriotic. Each state decides who its citizens are. In Ethiopia, citizenship comes mainly by descent, and no Ethiopian can lose it against his or her will.

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: A citizen has specific rights and obligations under the laws of a country.
Citizenship is both a legal status and a personal identity.
Family, community, friends and teachers teach us good citizenship.
Each state defines its own citizens, so laws on granting and losing citizenship differ.
Ethiopia enacted Africa's first written citizenship law in 1930 G.C. The FDRE Constitution (1995 G.C.) uses the right of descent or blood.

screens.why: These are the four features of a good citizen.

screens.text: Citizenship is a legal standing that comes with being a recognised member of a country.
screens.why: Citizenship is a legal status earned by being a registered member.

screens.text: Which principle does the FDRE Constitution use for Ethiopian citizenship?
screens.why: Article 6: both or either Ethiopian parents.
screens.clue: Is it about parents or land?

screens.text: Which statement is TRUE under Ethiopian law?
opts: Being born in Ethiopia always makes you a citizen
The government may remove citizenship against a person's will
A foreigner may be naturalized after meeting requirements such as four years' residence
Only people with two Ethiopian parents are citizens
screens.ans: A foreigner may be naturalized after meeting requirements such as four years' residence
screens.why: Ethiopia has no broad right of soil; involuntary loss is not allowed; one Ethiopian parent is enough. Naturalization with requirements is allowed.
screens.clue: Check each statement against what you learned in 1.3.

items.text: A citizen is a person who has certain rights but no obligations.
items.why: A citizen has rights and responsibilities.

items.text: Citizens are required to abide by the laws of their country and protect it against its enemies.
items.why: The book says citizens follow the rules and defend the country.
items.clue: What do citizens give in exchange?

items.text: To be a good citizen one must be irresponsible.
items.why: Responsibility is a feature of good citizenship.

items.text: All countries follow the same procedures in granting and loss of citizenship.
items.why: Each state defines its own rules.
items.clue: Who decides who a state's citizens are?

items.text: Citizenship is a legal standing that comes with being a recognized member of a country.
Which one of the following is CORRECT about citizenship?
opts: It refers to full and responsible membership of the state
A citizen is a person who holds the title of citizenship
items.why: All three are stated in the book.
items.clue: Check each option against the book.

items.text: Which one is NOT a feature of a good citizen?
opts: Willing to make sacrifices for the country
Does not show respect towards others
items.ans: Does not show respect towards others
items.clue: Which one is a bad habit?

items.text: In a diverse society, ___ is important for peaceful coexistence.
items.why: Tolerance allows us to live peacefully.

pairs: The principle of right of blood
Citizenship from people recognised as legal parents
Usually referred to as right of soil
A foreign national who marries a national acquires citizenship
items.why: Option D (involuntary loss) matches nothing: it is a way of losing citizenship.
items.clue: Soil = place of birth; blood = parents.

notes.text: Glossary: the Patriotism entry is garbled in the book ("the quality of being, devotion to and vigorous for one country"); shown as "devotion to and strong support for one's country". The Citizen entry also has a slip.
Review Part III has an extra option D (involuntary loss of citizenship) that matches nothing; it is explained in the why.
